tasks.short: Plan play corners and exploration activities for the theme, set them up, demonstrate and question in circle time, guide play, photograph children's work, check photo consent, and check and post photos to parents.

steps.what: Preschool teacher plans the theme's play corners, exploration table and circle activities

loop.input: The theme, the development goals chosen from the school's fixed list, the weeks available and the class's materials list.
loop.output: A theme plan with play-corner set-ups, exploration questions and circle activities per week.
loop.check: Every activity must name a goal code whose text it reflects; every chosen goal appears at least once; only materials on the class list are used; the teacher edits before use. No child data enters the draft.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the teacher plans alone.
loop.why_not_simpler: Inventing play situations that invite young children to observe and ask is creative work; a template gives only the grid.

steps.what: Preschool teacher sets up the play corners and exploration table
Preschool teacher gives a demonstration and asks children to observe and question in circle time
Preschool teacher guides children as they investigate during play and work time
Preschool teacher photographs children's work
Preschool teacher checks each child in the photos against the photo consent list
Preschool teacher checks the final post: photos, caption and the class group it goes to
Preschool teacher posts the approved photos to the class parents in the parent app

tasks.design: A bounded step drafts a theme plan with play-corner set-ups and exploration questions from the chosen goal codes, and the teacher edits it. In the parent app of the student information system ({OTHER}), the teacher tags the children in each photo and the app shows the consent status of each tagged child, instead of the teacher checking a paper list; no face recognition is used. The teacher then checks the final post and posts it to the class group. Photographing, setting up, demonstrating and guiding play stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Theme plans were written from scratch, and photo consent was checked against a paper list.
tasks.enabler_now: Language models draft plans that a goal-code check can verify; parent apps can hold photo consent per child.
tasks.still_hard: Drafts must fit the room, the materials and the children; use of planning assistants tends to fall off.
tasks.human_edge: Following a child's question and turning it into an investigation for the whole group.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; planning starts from a draft.

reach.learn: Whether written exploration questions help assistants guide children.

evidence.claim: Among 464 primary teachers, a lesson assistant cut weekly preparation from 3.3 to 2.5 hours, but covered 7% of lessons and use declined (randomised, independent evaluation).
A Dutch practice product drafts a class activity for a lesson goal.
Photos of children need parents' consent under the GDPR.

assumptions: Boundary: from planning a theme to sharing children's work; assessment is outside.
Input contract: goal list set by the school; photo consent per child recorded by the school administrator from the enrolment form; fallback is planning by hand and the paper consent list.
No child data enters the drafting step.
Set-up, circle time and play do not change.
Capture, consent check and posting are separate steps: s6 keeps 40 because the teacher still tags each child; the final check and the post keep their full time.
s1 keeps 70 because the teacher still chooses and rewrites the activities; the draft saves looking up set-ups and questions.
unknowns: Whether photo consent is recorded digitally.
research_questions: Do drafted exploration questions change how children talk during play?

already_counted.description: Preschool teacher edits the drafted theme plan.

incremental.description: Preschool teacher notes theme goals and materials for the draft.

approvals.approved_version: The photos and caption exactly as checked by the preschool teacher in s7, posted once to the named class group in the parent app, showing only children with photo consent; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the teacher reuses last year's themes and changes little in the draft, so planning keeps 90 (2.8); high: new themes planned from the draft (5.8).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Check who collects each child, register attendance and absence, apply medicine and photo rules, enforce class rules and report absence.

steps.what: Preschool teacher checks that the person collecting a child is on the authorised list
Parents phone or tell the teacher at the door that their child will be absent and why
Preschool teacher registers attendance and asks parents about absences
Preschool teacher applies the medicine and allergy protocol
Preschool teacher checks the paper photo consent list before sharing images
Preschool teacher enforces the rules governing students in class and on the playground
School administrator reports unexplained absence of school-age children to the attendance officer

tasks.design: The student information system ({OTHER}) shows each child's authorised collectors, photo consent and medicine agreement on the class tablet, and parents report absence with a reason in the parent app for the teacher to confirm. Checking at the door, applying the medicine protocol and enforcing rules stay with the teacher.
tasks.previous_blocker: Pick-up lists, consents and absence notes were on paper and in the teacher's head.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems hold pupil data and parent apps; tablets are common in early years.
tasks.still_hard: Judging an unknown collector or a sick child is a person's call; absence rules apply from the compulsory school age.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising when something about a pick-up is not right and stopping it calmly.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; checks are quicker and on hand.

reach.task: Keep pick-up lists and consents current
reach.learn: Whether parent-entered changes reduce admin calls.

evidence.claim: A Dutch pupil records system keeps pupil records and a parent app.
Parents have consent rights on the school's pupil-data rules.
Children must attend school from age five under national rules, and unexplained absence is reported.

assumptions: Boundary: from arrival and pick-up checks to absence reported; safeguarding procedures are outside.

Input contract: authorised collectors, photo consent and medicine agreements entered by the school administrator from parents' forms; absence reasons entered by parents in the app; fallback is paper lists.
Administrator and parent time is outside the teacher's savings.
Door checks, medicine and rules do not change.

Input contract for s2: absence reasons entered by parents in the parent app (s7, share 1), with about the effort of today's call; children not reported are still asked about by the teacher. Registering who is present is a first record and keeps its time, so s2 keeps 70: only asking parents about absences shrinks.
unknowns: Share of parents who report absence through the app.
How pick-up lists are kept today.
research_questions: Do app absence reports cut morning phone calls?

incremental.description: Preschool teacher passes on changes parents mention at the door.
School administrator keeps pick-up lists, consents and medicine agreements current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: few parents report absence in the app, so s2 keeps 90 (13.7); high: most parents use the app (17.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Spot children who need extra help, discuss them with the support coordinator, write and agree a support plan, run extra sessions and evaluate.

steps.what: Preschool teacher reviews the progress-per-goal view of observations and screening results
Preschool teacher identifies children requiring extra help
Preschool teacher discusses each child with the internal support coordinator
Preschool teacher writes the support plan with goals and activities

loop.input: The teacher's notes from the talk with the support coordinator, the child's goals per area from the records, and the school's intervention library.
loop.output: A support plan with two or three goals, activities from the library, frequency and an evaluation date.
loop.check: Each goal must map to a development goal code and be supported by a recorded observation; activities must come from the library; no diagnostic labels; the teacher signs before the plan is saved.
loop.stop: One draft and one redraft; then the teacher writes the plan.
loop.why_not_simpler: Turning talk notes into goals and a coherent plan is writing; a form only gives the headings.

steps.what: Preschool teacher discusses the plan with the parents
Preschool teacher implements the remedial programs in extra small-group sessions
Preschool teacher gathers the observations recorded since the plan started
Preschool teacher evaluates the plan after six weeks against its goals
Internal support coordinator reviews plans and evaluations

tasks.design: A progress-per-goal view in the student information system ({OTHER}) shows which children lag on which goals. A bounded step drafts the support plan from the teacher's notes and the school's intervention library inside the school's approved environment, and the teacher signs it; the evaluation view pulls observations recorded since the plan started.
tasks.previous_blocker: Plans were written from scratch and evaluations rebuilt from scattered notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Pupil records systems track goals; a Dutch research project is building AI drafting of support plans, with no results yet.
tasks.still_hard: Support notes can be health data; drafts must avoid labels and fit what the teacher can deliver.
tasks.human_edge: Finding the small step a struggling child can take next and keeping parents on board.

ambition.what: Every plan evaluated on its date with recorded observations, not when there is time.

tasks.altitude: The teacher signs drafted plans and spends the time on sessions; decisions stay with the teacher and the support coordinator.

reach.learn: Whether the same draft-and-sign pattern meets the stricter legal plan.

evidence.claim: A Dutch research project will draft the justification in pupils' development plans against quality criteria; no results yet.
A Dutch pupil records system includes a development plan module and learning-goal tracking.
Support needs can be health data under the GDPR, and new pupil-data processing needs a DPIA.
A formal development plan is set within six weeks of enrolment after consulting parents and evaluated yearly.

assumptions: Boundary: from spotting a need to the plan evaluated; formal development plans for heavy needs are outside.

Input contract: observations per goal recorded by teachers; intervention library kept by the support coordinator; drafting runs in the school's approved environment under a processing agreement; fallback is writing by hand.
Support coordinator and parent time is outside the teacher's savings.
Talks and extra sessions do not change.
s4 keeps 70 because the teacher reads every drafted goal and activity against the observations and rewrites what does not fit before signing.
unknowns: Number of children with a support plan per class.
research_questions: Do drafted plans meet the support coordinator's quality criteria as often as hand-written ones?

already_counted.description: Preschool teacher checks and signs the drafted plan.
Preschool teacher reviews the progress-per-goal view.

incremental.description: Preschool teacher writes the talk notes the draft needs.
Support coordinator keeps the intervention library current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the school does not approve the drafting tool, so the plan is written by hand and s4 keeps its full time (10.0); high: drafting used as designed (16.3).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Plan the week with the parallel colleague, keep one shared plan, check it against goals, book rooms and helpers, and brief the assistant.

steps.what: Preschool teacher meets the parallel colleague to plan and schedule lessons and themes
Preschool teacher copies the agreed plan into the class planning document
Preschool teacher checks the plan covers the approved curriculum goals
Preschool teacher books the gym hall, shared activities and parent helpers by message
Preschool teacher briefs the teaching assistant about the week
Team leader checks the year plan for the early-years group

tasks.design: Both teachers plan in one shared planning document in {DOCS} during their meeting, with activities tagged by goal code so coverage of the approved curriculum is shown automatically. Gym hall, shared activities and parent helpers are booked in a shared {CALENDAR}; the planning talk and the assistant's briefing stay as they are.
tasks.previous_blocker: Agreements were copied from meeting notes into separate class plans and coverage was checked by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Shared documents and calendars are standard; goal tags make coverage a simple count.
tasks.still_hard: Agreeing a week that suits two different groups is a conversation.
tasks.human_edge: Sharing ideas with a colleague and knowing what your own group needs this week.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in decision rights; one plan instead of two copies.

reach.learn: Whether the shared plan lets assistants prepare without a briefing.

evidence.claim: Shared documents and calendars with tags are standard school tooling.
Staff have consent rights on tools that can monitor them.

assumptions: Boundary: from the planning talk to the assistant briefed; teaching is outside.
Input contract: goal codes from the school's list; activity tags added by the teachers; room calendar kept by the administrator; fallback is separate plans.
Team leader time is outside the teacher's savings.
The planning talk and briefing do not change.
unknowns: Whether the parallel classes plan together today.
How rooms and helpers are booked now.
research_questions: Do goal tags reveal goals the early-years team rarely covers?

incremental.description: Preschool teacher tags activities with goal codes.
Team leader keeps the goal codes current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the teachers keep separate notes and copy part of the plan afterwards, and helpers still arrange by message, so s2 keeps 60 and s4 keeps 80 (21.1); high: one shared plan and the shared calendar used as designed (31.1).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The preschool teacher keeps play, care, rules and relationships; plans, checks and bookings become drafts and shared tools.
role.ambitious_version: A preschool teacher who evaluates every support plan on time and plans the week in one shared place.
